entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Irrigation Methods and Application Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Basin | Field that is level in all directions, encompassed by a dike to prevent runoff, and provides an undirected flow of water onto the field
Basin irrigation | Type of surface irrigation where water is applied to the basin through a gap in the perimeter dike or adjacent ditch; water is retained until it infiltrates into the soil or the excess is drained off
Border irrigation | Method of irrigation which makes use of parallel border strips where the water flows down the slope at a nearly uniform depth
Border strip | Area of land bounded by two border ridges or dikes that guide the irrigation stream from the inlet point of application to the ends of the strip
Furrows | Small parallel channels, made to carry water in order to irrigate the crop
Furrow irrigation | Method of irrigation where water runs through small parallel channels as it moves down the slope of the field
Drip irrigation | Trickle irrigation; involves dripping water onto the soil at very low rates (2-20 litres/hour) from emitters where water is applied close to plants so that only part of the soil in which the roots grow is wetted
Sprinkler irrigation | Method of applying irrigation water similar to natural rainfall where water is distributed through a system of pipes by pumping and then sprayed into the air through sprinklers so that it breaks up into small water drops which fall to the ground
Surface irrigation system | Application of water by gravity flow to the surface of the field; either the entire field is flooded (basin irrigation) or the water is fed into small channels (furrows) or strips of land (borders)
Head ditch | Supply ditch; small channel along one part of a field that is used for distributing water in surface irrigation
Farm ditch | Channel which conveys irrigation water from the turnout to the paddy field
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of irrigation application methods and related surface-irrigation terms.

entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Open Channel Hydraulics Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Area | Cross-sectional area of the flow which is measured perpendicular to the direction of flow
Channel bed slope | Inclination or elevation drop per unit length of the channel bottom
Critical depth | Depth of water flow where the energy content is at minimum, hence no other backwater forces are involved
Depth | Depth of water in the channel cross-section
Energy grade line | Specific energy line; grade line of the water surface profile plus the velocity head in open channels
Hydraulic depth | Ratio of flow area to the wetted top width
Hydraulic grade line | Hydraulic gradient; profile of the free water surface
Hydraulic jump | Occurs when a thin sheet of incoming flow moving at high velocity strikes water of sufficient depth
Hydraulic radius | Cross-sectional area of flow divided by the wetted perimeter
Normal depth | Constant flow depth along a longitudinal section of a channel under a uniform flow condition
Open channel flow | Water flow that is conveyed in such a manner that the top surface is exposed to the atmosphere, such as flow in canals, ditches, drainage channels, culverts, and pipes under partially full flow conditions
Side slope | Ratio of the horizontal to vertical dimension of the channel wall
Slope of the energy grade line | Slope of the water surface profile plus the velocity head in open channels
Slope of the hydraulic grade line | Slope of the free water surface
Top width | Width of the channel cross-section at the free surface
Uniform flow | Occurs when flow has a constant water area, depth, discharge, and average velocity through a reach of channel
Wetted perimeter | Portion of the perimeter of the canal that is in contact with the flowing water
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of open channel and hydraulic terms.

entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Canal and Conveyance Structure Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Drop | In-line canal structure designed to convey canal water from a higher level to a lower level, duly dissipating the excess energy resulting from the drop in elevation
Invert | Inside bottom or sill of the conduit
Inverted siphon | Closed conduit designed to convey canal water in full and under pressure running condition, to convey canal water by gravity under roadways, railways, drainage channels and local depressions
Elevated flume | Water conveying conduit or trough which is supported on abutments by piers
Road crossing | Conveys canal water under roads or railroads
Equipment crossing | Provision for passing of equipment and small machinery
Lined channel | Lined canal; canals with impermeable material (usually concrete) for channel stabilization and/or reduced seepage
Unlined channels | Unlined canal; canals that are cut through the soil, in which the soil excavated from the bed is used to form the embankment
Diversion dam | Structure or weir provided across the river or creek to raise its water level and divert the water into the main canal to facilitate irrigation by gravity
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of canal and conveyance structure terms.

entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Crop Water Requirement and Irrigation Efficiency Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Actual crop evapotranspiration | Rate of evapotranspiration equal to or smaller than predicted crop evapotranspiration as affected by the level of available soil water, salinity, field size or other causes
Application efficiency | Ratio of the average depth of irrigation water infiltrated and stored in the root zone to the average depth of irrigation water applied
Conveyance efficiency | Ratio between water received at the inlet for a block of fields to that released at the project's headwork
Conveyance loss | Loss of water from a channel during transport due to seepage and percolation
Crop coefficient | Ratio of the actual crop evapotranspiration to its potential evapotranspiration
Crop evapotranspiration | Rate of evapotranspiration of a disease-free crop growing in a large field under optimal soil conditions, including sufficient water and fertilizer, achieving full production potential under the given growing environment
Cropping pattern | Sequence of different crops grown in regular order on any particular field or fields
Crop water requirements | Amount of water used in producing crops which is the sum of evapotranspiration or consumptive use plus seepage and percolation losses
Diversion water requirement | Total quantity of water diverted from a stream, lake, or reservoir, or removed from the ground in order to irrigate a crop
Effective rainfall | Amount of rainwater that falls directly on the field and is used by the crop for growth and development, excluding deep percolation, surface runoff and interception
Effective rooting depth | Soil depth from which the bulk of the roots of the crop extracts most of the water needed for evapotranspiration
Evapotranspiration | Combination of water transpired from vegetation and evaporated from the soil, water, and plant surfaces
Farm water requirement | Amount of water to replenish the crop water requirement and losses less the effective rainfall
Land preparation water requirement | Amount of water required in lowland rice production which includes water losses through evaporation, seepage and percolation and land soaking
Land soaking water requirement | Amount of water required in lowland rice production which is a function of the initial soil moisture and the physical properties of the soil
Pan coefficient | Ratio between reference evapotranspiration and water loss by evaporation from an open water surface of a pan
Pan evaporation | Rate of water loss by evaporation from an open water surface of a pan
Percolation | Vertical flow of water to below the root zone, affected by soil structure, texture, bulk density, mineralogy, organic matter content, salt type and concentration
Reference crop evapotranspiration | Rate of evapotranspiration from a reference surface: a hypothetical reference crop with an assumed crop height of 0.2 m, a fixed surface resistance of 70 s/m and an albedo of 0.23
Residual moisture content | Moisture left in the soil before the initial irrigation water delivery, describing the extent of water depletion from the soil when the water supply has been cut off
Distribution uniformity | Numerical value on the uniformity of application for agricultural irrigation systems
Irrigation period | Time required to cover an area with one application of water
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of crop water requirement and irrigation efficiency terms.

entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Dam, Embankment and Reservoir Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Active storage | Volume of water stored in reservoir between the minimum water level and normal water level
Afflux elevation | Rise in maximum flood level from the original unobstructed flood level which results after an obstruction to the flow, such as a dam, has been introduced
Dam | Any barrier constructed to store water
Dam height | Vertical distance from lowest point of the ground line to the dam crest
Dead storage | Volume below the intake structure; sediment volume based on 25 years of accumulation in the reservoir
Designed height | Actual height of the embankment after settlement
Finished height | Height of the embankment to be attained during construction
Freeboard | Additional height of the dam provided as a safety factor to prevent overtopping by wave action or other causes
Homogeneous embankment | Dam composed of a single kind of embankment material exclusive for slope protection
Inside slope | Slope of the upstream face of the embankment
Outside slope | Slope at the downstream face of the embankment
Natural spillway | Spillway which is not excavated, such as a natural draw, saddle or drainage way
Normal storage elevation | Maximum elevation of the water surface which can be attained by the dam or reservoir without flow in the spillway
Reservoir | Part of the system that impounds the runoff
Spillway | Channel which releases surplus or flood water which cannot be contained in the active storage space of the reservoir
Storage capacity | Total capacity at normal water surface elevation
Storage ratio | Ratio of the storage capacity to the total earth volume required for embankment construction, indicating the relative cost of different reservoir types
Structural height | Vertical distance measured from the top of the dam down to the bedrock
Upstream face | Side of the embankment wetted by the impounded water
Zoned embankment | Dam consisting of a central impervious core flanked between zones of more pervious materials
Well-protected reservoir | Reservoir where the upper reaches of the basin is shielded by high mountain barriers
Bearing capacity | Maximum average contact pressure between the foundation and the soil which should not produce shear failure in the soil
Filter drain | Dam component which prevents migration of small particles and screens off fine materials that flow with seepage water and prevent piping
Watershed | Area which contributes runoff or drains water into the reservoir
Water balance | Accounting of water inflows, such as irrigation and rainfall, and outflows, such as evaporation, seepage and percolation
Water right | Privilege granted by the government to use and appropriate water
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of dam, embankment and reservoir terms.

entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Groundwater and Soil Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Aquifer | Geologic formation which contains water and transmits it at a rate sufficient to be economically developed for pumping by an artificially developed well
Confined aquifer | Groundwater that is confined by a relatively impermeable layer
Unconfined aquifer | Aquifer which has a water table serving as the upper surface of the zone of saturation
Shallow tubewell | Tube or shaft vertically set into the ground at a depth that is usually less than 15 m for the purpose of bringing groundwater into the soil surface, whose pumps are set above the water level
Well log | Record of formation stratification of an aquifer showing the depth, thickness, degree of consolidation and other aquifer physical characteristics
Karst topography | Geological formation shaped by the dissolution of a layer or layers of soluble bedrock, usually carbonate rocks such as limestone or dolomite
Permeability test | Method to determine the rate of flow under laminar flow conditions through a unit cross-sectional area of soil under unit hydraulic gradient
Effective size | Particle diameter corresponding to a 10% sieve passing
Uniformity coefficient | Ratio of the particle size at 60% passing to that at 10% passing
Design irrigable area | Maximum area which an irrigation project can serve, considering the extent of arable lands and the available water supply
Potential irrigable area | Area capable of being irrigated, principally as regards availability of water, suitable soils, and topography of land
Hydrologic frequency analysis | Estimation of the chance or likelihood of occurrence of a given event by determining the frequency curves of best fit to samples of hydrologic data
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of groundwater and soil terms.

entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Water Quality and Wastewater Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Access areas | Areas open for public entry, such as golf courses, public and private parks, playgrounds, schoolyards and playing fields, residential landscapes and industrial park landscapes
Restricted areas | Areas with limited entry, such as freeway landscape, highway medians and other similar areas
Algal bloom | Overgrowths of algae in water producing dangerous toxins in fresh or marine water
Contamination | Introduction of substances not found in the natural composition of water that make the water less desirable or unfit for intended use
Effluent | Discharges from known sources which is passed into a body of water or land, or wastewater flowing out of a manufacturing/industrial plant including domestic, commercial and recreational facilities
Effluent standard | Any legal restriction or limitation on quantities, rates, and/or concentrations of physical, chemical or biological parameters of effluent which a person or point source is allowed to deliver into a body of water or land
Loading limit | Allowable pollutant-loading limit per unit of time which the wastewater generator is permitted to discharge into any receiving body of water or land
Pollutant | Any substance, whether solid, liquid, gaseous or radioactive, which directly or indirectly alters the quality of any segment of the receiving water body or land resource, or is hazardous or in excess of allowable limits
Re-use | Taking wastewater from one industry or process, treating it and then using it in another process or industry, such as for irrigation, as liquid fertilizer and for aquaculture
Setback distance | Distance from the perimeter of the irrigation area to the community or area of concern that is sensitive to contamination
Waste | Any material, either solid, liquid, semi-solid, contained gas or other forms, resulting from industrial, commercial, mining, or agricultural operations, or from community and household activities, that is devoid of usage and discarded
Wastewater | Waste in liquid state containing pollutants
Unimodal rainfall pattern | Rainfall pattern with five wet months of more than 200 mm/month, five dry months of less than 100 mm/month, two transition months of 100-200 mm/month, and total annual rainfall above 1500 mm
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of water quality, effluent and wastewater terms.

entries.title: PAES 601 — Table: Sprinkler and Drip/Micro-Irrigation Terminologies
entries.table_content:
Term | Definition
Emitters | Applicator used in drip, subsurface, or bubbler irrigation, designed to dissipate pressure and discharge a small uniform flow or trickle of water at a constant rate that does not vary significantly because of minor differences in pressure
Emitter spacing | Spacing between emitters or emission points along a lateral line
Manifold | Portion of the pipe network between the mainline and the laterals
Manufacturer's coefficient of variation | Measure of the variability of discharge of a random sample of a given make, model and size of emitter, as provided by the manufacturer before any field operations or aging has taken place, determined through a discharge test of a sample of 50 emitters under a set pressure
Optimal emitter spacing | Drip emitter spacing which is 80% of the wetted diameter estimated from field tests
Sprinkler spacing | Distance between two sprinkler heads along the lateral
Wetted diameter | Diameter of the circular area wetted by the sprinkler when operating at a given pressure and no wind
Wetted widths | Width of the strip that would be wetted by a row of emitters spaced at their optimal spacing along a single lateral line
entries.description: PAES 601:2016 General Irrigation Terminologies - definitions of sprinkler and drip/micro-irrigation terms.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Crop Water Requirement (CWR)
entries.variables: CWR = crop water requirement, mm/day; ETa = actual evapotranspiration, mm/day; (S&P)field = seepage and percolation in the field/service area, mm/day.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 - basic equation for crop water requirement, applicable to both lowland and upland crops.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Actual Evapotranspiration (ETa)
entries.variables: ETa = actual evapotranspiration, mm/day; ETo = reference evapotranspiration, mm/day; Kc = crop coefficient.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 - actual crop evapotranspiration is derived from reference evapotranspiration and the crop coefficient.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Farm Water Requirement (FWR)
entries.formula: FWR = CWR - ER + LPWR + farm ditch losses; or FWR = (CWR - ER + LPWR) / Ea
entries.variables: FWR = farm water requirement, mm; CWR = crop water requirement, mm; ER = effective rainfall, mm; LPWR = land preparation water requirement, mm; Ea = application efficiency.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 - farm water requirement equation (upland crops omit LPWR).

entries.title: PAES 602 — Land Preparation Water Requirement (LPWR)
entries.variables: LPWR = land preparation water requirement, mm; LSR = land soaking requirement, mm; SW = standing water, mm; ETo = reference evapotranspiration, mm.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 - land preparation water requirement for lowland rice.
entries.notes: The recommended value for standing water (SW) during land preparation is 10 mm.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Land Soaking Requirement (LSR)
entries.variables: LSR = land soaking requirement, mm; n = soil porosity; RMC = residual moisture content; As = apparent specific gravity; Drz = depth of root zone, mm.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 - land soaking requirement, detailed in Annex F using soil physical properties by texture.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Farm Ditch Losses
entries.formula: Farm ditch losses = (S&P)farm ditch x P x L
entries.variables: (S&P)farm ditch = seepage and percolation rate in farm ditch, mm/day; P = wetted perimeter, m; L = length of farm ditch, m.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 - seepage and percolation losses in farm ditches, determined per PAES 604/605 methods.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Diversion Water Requirement (DWR)
entries.formula: DWR = FWR + conveyance losses; or DWR = FWR / Ec
entries.variables: DWR = diversion water requirement, mm; FWR = farm water requirement, mm; Ec = conveyance efficiency.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 - diversion water requirement equation.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Seepage and Percolation Losses in Canals
entries.variables: (S&P)canals = seepage and percolation losses in the canals; Aw = wetted area = wetted perimeter x length of canal; S&P rate = rate of seepage and percolation.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Annex G - determination of conveyance losses in unlined canals.
entries.notes: Leakage through gates and left-over water in the canal is estimated as 5% of total farm water requirement; leakage through canal dikes is computed the same way as seepage and percolation losses in canals.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Reference Evapotranspiration, Penman-Monteith Method
entries.variables: ETo = reference evapotranspiration, mm/day; Delta = slope of vapor pressure curve, kPa/C; Rn = net radiation, MJ/m2/day; G = soil heat flux, MJ/m2/day; gamma = psychrometric constant, kPa/C; Tmean = mean daily air temperature, C; u2 = wind speed at 2 m height, m/s; es = saturation vapor pressure, kPa; ea = actual vapor pressure, kPa.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Annex B - Penman-Monteith method, reliable for any length period among the four ETo methods.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Reference Evapotranspiration, Radiation Method
entries.variables: ETo = reference evapotranspiration, mm/day; W = weighting factor for the effect of radiation on ETo (function of temperature and altitude, Table B.11); Rs = solar radiation expressed as mm/day equivalent.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Annex B - Radiation method, usable for periods of 5 days or more, less precise than Penman-Monteith.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Reference Evapotranspiration, Blaney-Criddle Method
entries.variables: ETo = reference evapotranspiration, mm/day; p = mean daily percentage of annual daytime hours (Table B.14, by latitude); Tmean = mean daily temperature, C.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Annex B - Blaney-Criddle method, usable for periods of 5 days or more.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Reference Evapotranspiration, Pan Evaporation Method
entries.variables: ETo = reference evapotranspiration, mm/day; Kp = pan coefficient; Epan = average pan evaporation, mm/day.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Annex B - Pan evaporation method using Class A pan or Colorado sunken pan.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Net Radiation Components (Penman-Monteith Method)
entries.formula: Rs = (0.25 + 0.50 n/N) Ra; Rso = [(0.75+2*Altitude)/100000] x Ra; Rns = 0.77 Rs; Rn = Rns - Rnl
entries.variables: Rs = solar radiation, MJ/m2/day; Ra = extraterrestrial radiation, MJ/m2/day (Table B.7, by latitude/month); n = actual duration of sunshine, h; N = mean daylight hours (Table B.8); Rso = clear-sky solar radiation; Rns = net solar (shortwave) radiation; Rnl = net longwave radiation (function of Tmax, Tmin, ea and Rs/Rso); Rn = net radiation.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Annex B - component equations used to determine net radiation (Rn) for the Penman-Monteith ETo formula.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Annex A: Cropping Calendar Climate Types
entries.table_content:
Climate Type | Description
Type I | Two pronounced seasons: dry from November to April, wet the rest of the year. Covers the western part of Luzon, Mindoro, Negros and Palawan.
Type II | No dry season, with a very pronounced maximum rainfall from November to January. Covers Catanduanes, Sorsogon, eastern Albay, eastern/northern Camarines Norte, part of eastern Quezon, eastern Leyte and a large portion of eastern Mindanao.
Type III | No pronounced season; relatively dry from November to April and wet the rest of the year. Covers western Mountain Province, southern Quezon, Bontoc Peninsula, Masbate, Romblon, northeast Panay, eastern Negros, central/southern Cebu, part of northern Mindanao and most of eastern Palawan.
Type IV | Rainfall more or less evenly distributed throughout the year. Covers Batanes Province, northeastern Luzon, western Camarines Norte and Sur, Albay, eastern Mindoro, Marinduque, western Leyte, northern Negros and most of central, eastern and southern Mindanao.
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Annex A (Informative) - climate type classification used to select recommended cropping calendars.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Table B.1: Duration and Accuracy of ETo Estimation Methods
entries.table_content:
Method | Duration | Accuracy/Reliability
Penman-Monteith | daily, monthly, seasonal | reliable for any length period
Radiation | period of 5 days or more | less precise than Penman-Monteith
Blaney-Criddle | period of 5 days or more | less precise than Penman-Monteith
Pan evaporation | period of 10 days or longer | less reliable for short-term estimates than other methods; can be accurate if evaporation pans are well maintained and properly located
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Table B.1 - comparison of the four reference evapotranspiration calculation methods, source: National Engineering Handbook, 1993.

entries.title: PAES 602 — Table B.2: Climatic Data Requirements by ETo Method
entries.table_content:
Method | Data Required
Penman-Monteith | maximum temperature, minimum temperature, wind speed at 2m, dewpoint temperature, maximum relative humidity, minimum relative humidity, actual duration of sunshine
Radiation | maximum temperature, minimum temperature, solar radiation
Blaney-Criddle | maximum temperature, minimum temperature
Pan evaporation | pan evaporation
entries.description: PAES 602:2016 Table B.2 - climatic data required for each ETo estimation method.

entries.title: PAES 603 — Manning's Equation for Channel Sizing
entries.variables: Q = discharge, m3/s; n = Manning's roughness coefficient; S = bed slope; A = cross-sectional area, m2; P = wetted perimeter, m.
entries.description: PAES 603:2016 Section 5.4.2 - used by trial and error to compute bed width and channel depth for a given design discharge.

entries.title: PAES 603 (A) — Rectangular Channel Geometry
entries.formula: A = by; P = b + 2y; R = by/(b+2y); T = b; D = y
entries.variables: A = area, m2; P = wetted perimeter, m; R = hydraulic radius, m; T = top width, m; D = hydraulic depth, m; b = bottom width, m; y = flow depth, m.
entries.description: PAES 603:2016 Annex A.1 - geometric relations for a rectangular canal cross-section.

entries.title: PAES 603 (A) — Trapezoidal Channel Geometry
entries.formula: A = (b+zy)y; P = b + 2y*sqrt(1+z^2); R = (b+zy)y / [b+2y*sqrt(1+z^2)]; T = b + 2zy; D = (b+zy)y / (b+2zy)
entries.variables: A = area, m2; P = wetted perimeter, m; R = hydraulic radius, m; T = top width, m; D = hydraulic depth, m; b = bottom width, m; y = flow depth, m; z = side slope ratio (horizontal:vertical).
entries.description: PAES 603:2016 Annex A.2 - geometric relations for a trapezoidal canal cross-section, the recommended shape for irrigation canals.

entries.title: PAES 603 (A) — Triangular Channel Geometry
entries.formula: A = zy^2; P = 2y*sqrt(1+z^2); R = zy / [2*sqrt(1+z^2)]; T = 2zy; D = y/2
entries.variables: A = area, m2; P = wetted perimeter, m; R = hydraulic radius, m; T = top width, m; D = hydraulic depth, m; y = flow depth, m; z = side slope ratio.
entries.description: PAES 603:2016 Annex A.3 - geometric relations for a triangular canal cross-section.

entries.title: PAES 603 (A) — Circular Channel Geometry
entries.formula: A = (1/8)(theta - sin(theta))d0^2; P = (1/2)theta*d0; R = (1/4)(1 - sin(theta)/theta)d0; T = sin(theta/2)d0 = 2*sqrt[y(d0 - y)]
entries.variables: A = area, m2; P = wetted perimeter, m; R = hydraulic radius, m; T = top width, m; d0 = conduit diameter, m; theta = angle subtended by the water surface at the center, radians; y = flow depth, m.
entries.description: PAES 603:2016 Annex A.4 - geometric relations for a circular conduit flowing partially full.

entries.title: PAES 603 (A) — Parabolic Channel Geometry
entries.variables: A = area, m2; P = wetted perimeter, m; R = hydraulic radius, m; T = top width, m; D = hydraulic depth, m; y = flow depth, m.

entries.title: PAES 604 — Change in Water Depth (deltaH)
entries.variables: deltaH = change in water depth in the pond at a given time interval, m; Hi = initial reading of water depth in the pond, m; Hf = final reading of water depth in the pond, m.
entries.description: PAES 604:2016 Section 9.1 - change in pond water depth used in the ponding method for seepage and percolation determination.

entries.title: PAES 604 — Average Pond Length and Width
entries.formula: Lave = (Li + Lf)/2; Wi = (Wi1+Wi2+Wi3)/3; Wf = (Wf1+Wf2+Wf3)/3; Wave = (Wi + Wf)/2
entries.variables: Lave = average wetted length of the pond, m; Li, Lf = pond length during initial and final reading, m; Wi1, Wi2, Wi3 = wetted pond width at three points during the initial reading, m; Wf1, Wf2, Wf3 = wetted pond width at three points during the final reading, m; Wi, Wf = average pond width during initial and final reading, m; Wave = average pond width at a given time interval, m.
entries.description: PAES 604:2016 Sections 9.2-9.3 - averaging formulas for pond length and width, based on measurements at a minimum of three points along the pond section.

entries.title: PAES 604 — Volume Loss (Vloss)
entries.formula: Vloss = (deltaH + R) x Lave x Wave
entries.variables: Vloss = total volume loss at a given time interval, m3; deltaH = change in water depth in the pond, m; R = amount of rainfall at a given time interval, m; Lave = average wetted length of the pond, m; Wave = average pond width, m.
entries.description: PAES 604:2016 Section 9.4 - total volume loss in the ponding method.

entries.title: PAES 604 — Seepage and Percolation Loss Rate
entries.formula: (S&P)losses = (Vloss/deltaT) / Lave; or (S&P)losses = [(deltaH + R) x Wave] / deltaT
entries.variables: (S&P)losses = seepage and percolation loss rate, m3/s-m; Vloss = total volume loss, m3; deltaT = time interval between the initial and final reading, s; Lave = average wetted length of the pond, m; deltaH = change in water depth, m; R = rainfall amount, m; Wave = average pond width, m.
entries.description: PAES 604:2016 Section 9.5 - seepage and percolation loss rate, expressed per unit length of channel.

entries.title: PAES 604 — Percent Seepage and Percolation Loss
entries.variables: %(S&P)losses = percent seepage and percolation loss; (S&P)losses = seepage and percolation loss rate, m3/s-m; Qdesign = design flow in the channel.
entries.description: PAES 604:2016 Section 9.6 - percent seepage and percolation loss relative to the channel's design flow.

entries.title: PAES 605 — Sharp-Edged Orifice Discharge
entries.formula: Q = Cd Cv A sqrt(2g(h1 - h2)) = Cd Cv A sqrt(2g*deltah)

entries.title: PAES 606 — Conduit Area from Orifice Formula (Road Crossing)

entries.title: PAES 606 — Conduit Velocity (RCP and Box Culvert)
entries.formula: Vp = Q / Ap (RCP); Vb = Q / Ab (box culvert)
entries.variables: Vp = velocity in the RCP, m/s; Vb = velocity in the box culvert, m/s; Q = canal discharge, m3/s; Ap, Ab = RCP and box culvert cross-sectional area, m2.
entries.description: PAES 606 - velocity check for road-crossing conduits against the maximum allowable velocity in Table 2.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Total Head Loss for Road Crossing / Inverted Siphon
entries.formula: hLT = 1.10 (hLi + hLv + hLo) [road crossing]; hLT = 1.10 (hLi + hLv + hb + htr + hLo) [inverted siphon]
entries.variables: hLT = total head loss, m; hLi = inlet transition loss, m; hLv = conduit friction loss, m; hb = bend loss, m; htr = trashrack loss, m; hLo = outlet transition loss, m.
entries.description: PAES 606 - total head loss shall be less than or equal to the available head; otherwise a different conduit size shall be adopted.
entries.notes: A 10% safety margin (factor 1.10) is applied to the sum of individual losses.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Vertical Drop: Critical Depth and Basin Length
entries.formula: hva = Va^2/2g; HE = da + hva; dc = (2/3)HE; y = CBu/s - CBd/s + dc; t = sqrt(2y/9.8); x = Vc x t; L = 2x + 0.30
entries.variables: hva = headloss due to upstream canal velocity, m; Va = upstream velocity, m/s; HE = height of drop, m; da = water depth upstream, m; dc = critical depth, m; CBu/s, CBd/s = canal bed elevation upstream/downstream, m; Vc = critical velocity, m/s; L = basin length, m.
entries.description: PAES 606 - design equations for the critical depth and stilling basin length of a vertical drop structure.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Vertical Drop Discharge Check
entries.variables: Q = discharge, m3/s; b = canal width, m; HE = height of drop, m.
entries.description: PAES 606 - discharge check for a vertical drop; if significantly different from the canal design discharge, the width shall be adjusted.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Rectangular Inclined Drop: Basin Width and Critical Depth
entries.formula: b = 18.48 sqrt(Q) / (Q + 9.92); q = Q/b; dc = cbrt(q^2/g)
entries.variables: b = basin width, m; Q = canal discharge, m3/s; q = canal discharge per unit width, m2/s; dc = critical depth, m.
entries.description: PAES 606 - sizing equations for the basin width and critical depth of a rectangular inclined drop.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Length of Stilling Pool (Rectangular Inclined Drop)
entries.formula: F = V/sqrt(g d1); if F <= 4.5, Lp = 3.5 d1; if 4.5 < F < 9, Lp = 4 d1; if F >= 9, Lp = 5 d2
entries.variables: F = Froude number; V = velocity, m/s; d1 = depth at the toe of the inclined channel, m; d2 = sequent (tailwater) depth, m; Lp = length of pool, m.
entries.description: PAES 606 - length of the stilling pool for a rectangular inclined drop, selected based on the Froude number regime.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Baffled Apron Drop: Chute Width and Baffle Height
entries.formula: B = Q/q; dc = cbrt(q^2/g); hb = 0.9 dc
entries.variables: B = chute width, m; Q = canal discharge, m3/s; q = discharge per meter width of chute, m3/m (Table 5); dc = critical depth, m; hb = height of baffle block, m.
entries.description: PAES 606 - sizing equations for a baffled apron drop chute and baffle blocks.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Inverted Siphon Bend Loss
entries.formula: hb = (0.124 + 3.104(S/2R)^(1/2)) x hvp x (theta/180) x number of bends
entries.variables: hb = bend loss, m; S = conduit width, m; R = radius along the center line, m; hvp = head loss due to velocity in the conduit, m; theta = deflection angle, degrees.
entries.description: PAES 606 - head loss due to bends in an inverted siphon conduit.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Inverted Siphon Trashrack Loss
entries.variables: htr = head loss due to trashrack, m; T = thickness of trashrack bars, cm; V = velocity below the trashrack, m/s; D = center-to-center spacing of bars, cm; A = inclination angle of the rack with the horizontal; B = angle of approach or horizontal inclination.

entries.title: PAES 606 — Elevated Flume Friction Slope and Critical Slope
entries.formula: Sf = Vf n / (Af/Pf)^(2/3); Sc = Vc nc / (Ac/Pc)^(2/3)
entries.variables: Sf = friction slope; Vf = actual velocity in the flume, m/s; n = design roughness coefficient; Af, Pf = computed flume area and perimeter, m2, m; Sc = critical slope; Vc = velocity in the flume based on critical depth, m/s; nc = 80% of design roughness coefficient; Ac, Pc = flume area/perimeter based on critical depth.
entries.description: PAES 606 - the computed friction slope of an elevated flume shall be greater than the critical slope (using 80% of design n); otherwise a different flume size shall be selected.

entries.table_content:
Selection Criteria | Furrow Irrigation | Border Irrigation | Basin Irrigation
Necessary development costs | Low | Moderate to high | High
Most appropriate field geometry | Rectangular | Rectangular | Variable
Soils | Coarse- to moderate-textured soils | Moderate- to fine-textured soils | Moderate- to fine-textured soils
Crops | Row crops (corn, vegetables, tree, sugarcane) | Row/solid-stand crops, annual crops (sugarcane, forage, pasture) | Solid-stand crops (paddy rice and others that can withstand waterlogged conditions)
Water supply | Low-discharge, long duration, frequent supply | Moderately high discharge, short duration, infrequent supply | High discharge, short duration, infrequent supply
Principal Risk | Erosion | Scalding | Scalding
Efficiency and uniformity | Relatively low to moderate | High with blocked ends | High
Slope | 0.05% to 3.0% | 2.0% to 5.0% | <= 0.1%
entries.description: PAES 607:2016 Design of Basin, Border and Furrow Irrigation Systems - comparative selection criteria for the three surface irrigation methods (NRCS-USDA, Part 623: Irrigation - National Engineering Handbook, 2012).

entries.title: PAES 607 — Gross Depth of Irrigation (Furrow)
entries.formula: d_gross = (Stream Size x Time Water Applied) / (Furrow Length x Wetted Furrow Spacing)
entries.variables: d_gross = gross depth of irrigation; Stream Size = furrow inflow rate; Time Water Applied = irrigation set time; Furrow Length = length of furrow, m; Wetted Furrow Spacing = spacing between furrows, m.
entries.description: PAES 607 - computation of the gross irrigation depth applied through a furrow irrigation system.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Required Discharge from Source (Furrow Irrigation)
entries.formula: Discharge from Source = Stream Size x Number of Furrows Flowing
entries.variables: Discharge from Source = total required supply, same units as stream size; Stream Size = flow rate delivered to a single furrow; Number of Furrows Flowing = number of furrows irrigated simultaneously.
entries.description: PAES 607 - total discharge required at the source to simultaneously irrigate a given number of furrows.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Basic Intake (Infiltration) Rate
entries.variables: fo = basic intake rate, m3/min/m; Qin = flow rate into the field, m3/min; Qout = flow rate out of the field, m3/min; L = furrow length, m.
entries.description: PAES 607 Annex A.7.2 - basic soil intake rate determined from inflow-outflow measurement along a test furrow.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Furrow Irrigation Application Efficiency
entries.formula: Ea = 100 x (Zreq x L) / (Qo x 60 x tco)
entries.variables: Ea = application efficiency, %; Zreq = soil moisture depletion measured x furrow spacing, m3/m; L = length of furrow, m; Qo = inlet discharge, m3/min/furrow; tco = cutoff time, s.
entries.description: PAES 607 Annex A.8.1 - application efficiency of a furrow irrigation system, i.e., the fraction of applied water stored in the root zone.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Tailwater Ratio and Deep Percolation Ratio
entries.formula: TWR = 100 x Vout / (Qo x 60 x tco); DPR = 100 - Ea - TWR
entries.variables: TWR = tailwater ratio, %; Vout = runoff volume per furrow, m3/furrow; Qo = inlet discharge, m3/min/furrow; tco = cutoff time, s; DPR = deep percolation ratio, %; Ea = application efficiency, %.
entries.description: PAES 607 Annex A.8.2-A.8.3 - evaluation of the fraction of applied irrigation water lost as surface runoff (tailwater) and as deep percolation.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Minimum Design Application Efficiency for Basin Irrigation
entries.description: PAES 607 - the minimum design application efficiency for basin irrigation; the minimum time to cover the basin shall be 60% of the time required for the net application depth to infiltrate the soil.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Basin Dike Freeboard
entries.description: PAES 607 - the settled height of a basin dike shall be at least equal to the gross application depth or the design maximum depth of flow, plus a freeboard of this percentage, whichever is greater.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Maximum Flow Velocity into a Basin
entries.description: PAES 607 - maximum water flow velocity allowed into a basin, to avoid scouring and erosion of the basin dikes/surface.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Basin Topography Tolerance
entries.description: PAES 607 - allowable difference between the highest and lowest elevations of a basin (shall be less than one-half of the net depth of application).

entries.title: PAES 607 — Maximum Basin Width and Flow Rate per Single Outlet
entries.description: PAES 607 - one outlet shall be installed for basin widths up to 60 m and flow rates up to 0.4 m3/s; multiple outlets may be used for larger basins/flows.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Minimum Furrow Grade
entries.description: PAES 607 - the minimum furrow grade to facilitate effective drainage following irrigation and excessive rainfall.

entries.title: PAES 607 — Default Furrow Stream Size
entries.description: PAES 607 - if furrows are not too long, this stream flow shall be adequate for irrigation (maximum stream size otherwise depends largely on furrow slope, see Table 5).

entries.title: PAES 607 — Soil Intake Rate Range Suitable for Border Irrigation
entries.description: PAES 607 - the soil shall have a moderately low to moderately high intake rate for border irrigation; extremely high (coarse sandy) and extremely low intake soils shall be avoided.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Net Depth of Water Application
entries.formula: d_net = (FC - PWP) x d_rz x MAD
entries.variables: d_net = net depth of water application, mm; FC-PWP = available moisture, mm/m; d_rz = depth of root zone, m; MAD = allowable moisture depletion, %.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 9.1 - used in the preliminary design of periodic-move and continuous-move sprinkler systems.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Irrigation Frequency at Peak Demand
entries.variables: I_f = irrigation frequency, day; d_net = net depth of water application, mm; peak ET_a = actual evapotranspiration at peak period, mm/day (per PAES 602:2016).
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 9.2.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Gross Depth of Water Application
entries.variables: d_gross = gross depth of water application, mm; d_net = net depth of water application, mm; E_a = application efficiency.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 9.3.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Preliminary System Capacity
entries.formula: Q_prelim = (10 x A x d_gross) / (I_f x N_shift x T)
entries.variables: Q_prelim = preliminary system capacity, m3/h; A = design area, ha; d_gross = gross depth of water application, mm; I_f = irrigation frequency, days; N_shift = number of shifts per day; T = irrigation time per shift, h.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 9.4.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Sprinkler Nozzle Discharge
entries.formula: q = S_l x S_m x r ; q = 0.00111 x C x d_n^2 x P^(1/2)
entries.variables: q = discharge of each sprinkler, m3/h; S_l = sprinkler spacing along the lateral, m; S_m = sprinkler spacing along the main, m; r = application rate, mm/h; C = coefficient of discharge; d_n = diameter of the nozzle orifice, mm; P = pressure at the nozzle, kPa.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.1.3 - theoretical nozzle discharge for sprinkler selection.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — System Capacity (periodic-move and continuous discharge total)
entries.formula: Q = N_c x N_s x q  (periodic-move, per shift);  Q = q x N  (total system, N = total number of sprinklers)
entries.variables: Q = system capacity, m3/h; N_c = number of laterals operating per shift; N_s = number of sprinklers per lateral; q = discharge of each sprinkler, m3/h; N = total number of sprinklers.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Sections 10.1.4 and 10.1.11.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Friction Loss in Main Lines (Hazen-Williams)
entries.variables: H_f = total friction loss in pipe with the same flow throughout, m; L = length of pipe, m; Q = total discharge, L/s; C = pipe roughness coefficient (145-150 for plastic pipe, 120 for aluminum pipe with couplers and new/coated steel pipe); D = inside diameter of pipe, mm.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.1.6.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Friction Loss in Laterals
entries.variables: h_f = friction loss in the lateral, m; H_f = total friction loss in pipe with the same flow throughout, m; F = correction factor depending on the number of outlets in the lateral (Table 5).
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.1.7.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Average Pressure Head and Sprinkler Pressure at Lateral Inlet
entries.formula: H_a = H_d + 0.26h_f + (S_e x L_L)/2 ; H_o = H_a + 0.74h_f + (S_e x L_L)/2
entries.variables: H_a = average sprinkler pressure of a lateral, m; H_d = sprinkler pressure at the distal end of the lateral, m; h_f = friction loss in the lateral, m; S_e = uniform slope of the lateral from the inlet (positive = uphill); L_L = lateral length, m; H_o = sprinkler pressure at the inlet to the lateral, m.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Sections 10.1.8 and 10.1.9.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Total Dynamic Head
entries.formula: TDH = H_n + H_m + H_j + H_s ; H_n = H_o + H_rh
entries.variables: TDH = total dynamic head against which the pump is working, m; H_n = head required at the junction of the lateral and the main, m; H_m = maximum friction loss in the main and suction line, m; H_j = elevation difference between the pump and the junction of the lateral and the main, m; H_s = elevation difference between the pump and the water supply after drawdown, m; H_o = sprinkler pressure at the inlet to the lateral, m; H_rh = riser height, m.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.1.10.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Pump Power Requirement
entries.variables: P = power requirement, kW; Q = system capacity, m3/h; TDH = total dynamic head against which the pump is working, m; E_p = pump efficiency from the pump performance chart.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Sections 10.1.12 and 10.2.8 (also used identically in Part B, Section 8.12).

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Maximum Allowable Flow Rate (Continuous-Move Systems)
entries.formula: I = (K x Q_sprinkler x 360) / [pi x (0.9R)^2 x w]
entries.variables: I = approximate infiltration rate or approximate sprinkler application rate, mm/hr; K = conversion constant, 3600; Q = sprinkler discharge, L/s; R = wetted radius of sprinkler, m; w = portion of circle receiving water, degrees.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.2.1 - the sprinkler application rate shall not exceed the soil's infiltration rate.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Travel Speed for Traveling Gun Sprinklers
entries.variables: v = travel speed, m/min; k = conversion constant, 60; Q = sprinkler discharge, L/s; d_gross = gross depth of water application, mm; W = tow-path spacing, m.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.2.4 - continuous-move (traveling gun) system design.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Maximum velocity in the main line
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.1.5.6 - the velocity in the main line of a sprinkler irrigation system shall be less than or equal to this value.

entries.title: PAES 608 (A) — Allowable friction loss in laterals
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part A, Section 10.1.5.5 - the allowable friction loss in the laterals of a sprinkler irrigation system.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Localized Evapotranspiration (Crop Water Requirement)
entries.formula: ET_crop-loc = ET_a x k_r  ; alternatively ET_crop-loc = ET_a x [0.1(P_d)^0.5]
entries.variables: ET_crop-loc = localized evapotranspiration, mm/day; ET_a = actual evapotranspiration, mm/day (per PAES 602:2016); k_r = ground cover reduction factor (Table 1); P_d = percentage ground cover (Keller and Bliesner formula).
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.1.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Leaching Requirement Ratio and Leaching Requirement
entries.formula: LR_t = EC_w / (2 x maxEC_e) ; IR_n = ET_crop-loc - R + LR ; LR = LR_t x (IR_n/E_a)
entries.variables: LR_t = leaching requirement ratio under drip irrigation; EC_w = electrical conductivity of irrigation water, dS/m; maxEC_e = electrical conductivity of saturated soil extract that reduces crop yield to zero, dS/m; IR_n = net irrigation requirement, mm/day; LR = leaching requirement, mm/day; R = rainfall, mm/day; E_a = application efficiency, %.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.2.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Gross Irrigation Requirement
entries.variables: IR_g = gross irrigation requirement, mm/day; ET_crop-loc = localized evapotranspiration, mm/day; E_a = application efficiency, %; R = rainfall, mm/day; LR = leaching requirement, mm/day.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.3.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Percentage Wetted Area
entries.formula: P_w = (100 x N_p x S_e x W) / (S_p x S_r)
entries.variables: P_w = percentage wetted area, %; N_p = number of emitters per plant; S_e = emitter spacing, m; W = wetted width along lateral, m; S_p = distance between plants within a row, m; S_r = row spacing, m.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.4.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Number of Emitters per Plant, Emitter Spacing, and Wetted Area
entries.formula: N_p = (Area per plant x P_w) / A_w ; S_e = S_p / N_p ; A_w = (pi x D^2) / 4
entries.variables: N_p = number of emitters per plant; P_w = percentage wetted area/100; A_w = area wetted by one emitter, m2; S_e = emitter spacing, m; S_p = distance between plants within a row, m; D = diameter of wetted area, m (Table 3).
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.5.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Irrigation Duration per Day
entries.variables: T_a = duration of irrigation per day, h; IR_g = gross irrigation requirement, mm/day; N_p = number of emitters per plant; q = emitter discharge, L/h.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.6.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Emitter Discharge-Pressure Relationship
entries.variables: q = emitter discharge, L/h; K_d = discharge coefficient characterizing the emitter; H = emitter operating pressure head, m; x = emitter discharge exponent (Table 4).
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.7.2 - a lower x means flow is less affected by pressure variations.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Design Emission Uniformity
entries.variables: EU = design emission uniformity, %; Cv = manufacturer's coefficient of variation; N_p = number of emitters per plant; q_m = minimum emitter discharge for minimum pressure in the sub-unit, L/h; q_a = average or design emitter discharge for the sub-unit, L/h.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.8.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Allowable Pressure Variation
entries.formula: delta_Hs = 2.5 x (H_a - H_m) ; H_m = H_a x (q_m/q_a)^(1/x)
entries.variables: delta_Hs = allowable pressure variation giving an EU reasonably close to the design value, m; H_a = pressure head giving the required q_a to satisfy EU, m; H_m = pressure head giving the required q_m to satisfy EU, m; q_m, q_a = emitter discharges, L/h; x = emitter discharge exponent.
entries.description: PAES 608:2016 Part B, Section 8.9.

entries.title: PAES 608 (B) — Drip emitter discharge rate range

entries.title: PAES 609 — Freeboard (Wave Run-up and Embankment Settlement)
entries.formula: Fb1 = 1.5 x (0.032 x sqrt(F x V) + 0.763 - 0.271 x F^(1/4)) ; Fb2 = 2% to 5% of dam height ; Fb = Fb1 + Fb2
entries.variables: Fb1 = freeboard due to wave run-up, m; F = reservoir effective fetch, km; V = wind velocity, km/h; Fb2 = freeboard due to embankment settlement, m; Fb = total freeboard, m.
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Section 7.1.1 - used to determine the total dam height together with dead storage, active storage, and flood surcharge.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Dam Crest Width
entries.variables: W1 = width of the dam crest, m; H1 = dam height, m; W2 = width of the dam crest, ft; H2 = dam height, ft. The minimum crest width for maintenance is 4 m; the largest computed dimension is adopted.
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Section 7.1.2.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Lag Time (Snyder's Synthetic Unit Hydrograph Method)
entries.formula: T_L = Ct x (L x Lc / sqrt(Y))^0.38
entries.variables: T_L = lag time, h; Ct = coefficient (1.2 for mountainous drainage area, 0.72 for foothill drainage area, 0.35 for valley drainage area); L = mainstream length from outlet to highest ridge, mi; Lc = mainstream length from outlet to nearest basin centroid, mi; Y = watershed gradient.
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex A, Section A.1.1.1 - used to derive the synthetic unit hydrograph for reservoir inflow estimation.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Time of Concentration and Time to Peak
entries.formula: Tc = T_L / 0.70 ; Tp = 0.5 x deltaD + T_L
entries.variables: Tc = time of concentration, h; T_L = lag time, h; Tp = time to peak, h; deltaD = standard rainfall duration, h (0.5 or 0.4 hr if Tc < 3; 1 hr if 3<Tc<6; 0.2 x Tc if Tc > 6).
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex A, Sections A.1.1.3 and A.1.1.4.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Peak Rate of Runoff
entries.variables: qp = peak rate of runoff, cm/mm; A = drainage area, km2; T_L = lag time, h.
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex A, Section A.1.1.5 - used to derive the synthetic unit hydrograph.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Initial Abstraction (Runoff Curve Number Method)
entries.variables: Ia = initial abstraction, in; s = maximum potential difference between rainfall and runoff, in; W = watershed index/runoff curve number (function of soil group, antecedent moisture condition, and land use cover).
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex A, Section A.1.5 - used to compute rainfall excess for the design flood inflow hydrograph.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Spillway Discharge (Broad-Crested Weir)
entries.formula: Q = C x L x H^(3/2)
entries.variables: Q = discharge over the spillway, m3/s; C = weir coefficient, 1.704; H = surcharge height, m; L = spillway width, m.
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex A, Section A.5.2.3 - spillway rating equation used in flood routing (maximum surcharge height allowed is 1 m).

entries.title: PAES 609 — Size of Rock or Stone for Slope Protection (Riprap)
entries.formula: d_m = 2.23 x C x H_w x [W/(G-W)] x sqrt[(1+S^2)/(S(S+2))]
entries.variables: d_m = riprap diameter, m; C = riprap factor (0.54 for hand-laced, 0.80 for dumped); H_w = wave height, m; W = unit weight of water, ton/m3; G = unit weight of stone, ton/m3; S = slope of embankment.
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex B, Section B.1.2 - sizing of upstream slope rock/riprap protection.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Filter Drain Design Equation
entries.formula: Q = (k x t^2 x w) / L
entries.variables: Q = design seepage value (equivalent to 5-10 times the estimated embankment seepage); k = average permeability of filter material; t = thickness of drain; L = length of drain; w = width of drain (perpendicular to flow).
entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex B, Section B.2.3 - sizing of the filter drain that prevents migration of fine soil particles and piping.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Froude Number for Stilling Basin Selection
entries.variables: F = Froude Number; V = velocity at entrance to the basin, m/s; g = gravitational acceleration, m/s2; d1 = depth of flow at the entrance to the basin, m.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Preliminary Discharge Pipe Diameter (Outlet Works)

entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex D, Section D.1.2 - sizing of the steel discharge pipe of the outlet works.

entries.title: PAES 609 — Impact-Type Energy Dissipator Basin Width
entries.formula: W = 2.85 x d_s x F x 0.58

entries.description: PAES 609:2016, Annex D, Section D.2.3 - sizing of the impact-type stilling basin at the outlet works.

entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex C, Table C.1 - allowable sliding factor by foundation material used to check dam stability against sliding.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Minimum Required Length of a Diversion Dam
entries.variables: Lmin = minimum required length of the dam, m. Q = maximum flood discharge, m3/s. qallow = allowable maximum flood concentration, m3/s/m (Table 2).
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.4 - minimum dam length based on foundation material's allowable flood concentration.
entries.notes: The minimum stable river width shall also be checked; the average of the two values is preferred for the final dam length.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Lacey's Formula for Minimum Dam Length
entries.variables: Pw = minimum required length of the dam, m. Q = maximum flood discharge, m3/s.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.4.2 - Lacey's regime formula, an alternative check for minimum diversion dam length.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Discharge Per Meter Run of Dam
entries.variables: qr = discharge per meter run, m3/s/m. Q = maximum flood discharge, m3/s. L = dam length, m.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.5.1 - used at the start of the afflux-elevation trial-and-error procedure.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Coefficient of Discharge for Flow Over a Submerged Dam
entries.variables: Cs = coefficient of discharge for flow over a submerged dam. Co = coefficient of discharge for free-flow condition (Figure 9). %Decrease = decrease in coefficient of discharge from Figure 10.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.5.5 - adjusts the free-flow discharge coefficient for tailwater submergence.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Discharge Equation for an Ogee Weir
entries.variables: qs = supplied discharge per meter run, m3/s/m. Cs = coefficient of discharge for flow over a submerged dam. H = head above the dam, m.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.5.6 - solved iteratively until qs equals the required qr, to establish the afflux elevation.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Hydraulic Jump Conjugate Depth
entries.variables: d2 = depth of water just downstream of the jump, m. d1 = assumed depth of water just upstream of the jump, m. v1 = velocity of water just upstream of the jump, m/s. g = gravitational acceleration, m/s2.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.6.3 - jump height (sequent/conjugate depth) computation for hydraulic jump analysis; may also be read from the nomograph in Figure 12.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Froude Number for Apron Length Selection
entries.variables: F = Froude number. v = water velocity. d = hydraulic depth. g = gravitational acceleration.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.7 - determines which basin type/apron-length formula in Table 3 applies.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Bottom Velocity for Riprap Sizing
entries.variables: vb = bottom velocity, ft/s. D = weighted mean diameter of river bed materials, in.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.10.1 - Berry's equation; the average tailwater velocity may be used if bottom velocity is unavailable.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Weight of Required Riprap Stone
entries.formula: WR = (4/3) x pi x r^3 x 165
entries.variables: WR = weight of riprap, lbs. r = required stone radius, ft.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.10.2 - riprap stone weight from the required radius (165 lb/ft3 assumed unit weight).
entries.notes: Riprap thickness shall be 1.5 times the stone diameter; gravel blanket thickness shall be half the riprap thickness but not less than 12 in.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Depth of Downstream Cut-off Wall
entries.variables: dco = required depth of the downstream cut-off wall, m. R = depth of scour, m (from Figure 14). dsupplied = supplied tailwater depth, m.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.11 - sizes the downstream cut-off wall against scour.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Ogee Crest Shape Equation
entries.variables: y = vertical distance from the apex of the crest. x = horizontal distance from the apex of the crest. H = difference between energy elevation and dam crest elevation. K, n = constants from the upstream face inclination and velocity of approach (Figure B3).
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex B - defines the downstream ogee crest profile fitted to the underside of a ventilated nappe.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Rational Formula for Flood Discharge
entries.formula: Q = F x C x IM x A
entries.variables: Q = flood discharge, m3/s. F = conversion factor. C = runoff coefficient of the catchment (Table A5). IM = rainfall intensity, mm/h. A = catchment area, km2.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex A.4 - flood discharge estimation method when streamflow records are unavailable.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Empirical Flood Formula (Rare and Occasional Flows)
entries.variables: Qrare = rare flow for a river with streamflow record, m3/s. Qoccasional = occasional flow for a river with streamflow record, m3/s. A = drainage area of the river with streamflow record, km2.
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex A.7 - the average of Qrare and Qoccasional is used as the flow estimate for rivers without streamflow records.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Height Range of a Diversion Dam
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 1 (Scope) - height range of the diversion dam type covered by the standard.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Minimum Length of Riprap
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Section 5.9 - minimum extent of riprap protection downstream of a diversion dam.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Horizontal Seismic Acceleration Coefficient
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex C.4.3.1 - horizontal acceleration applied at the dam's center of gravity for earthquake force analysis.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Factor of Safety Against Overturning
entries.value: 1.5 to 2 (may reduce to 1 with seismic forces)
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex C.2.1 - required factor of safety against overturning under normal stable conditions.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Assumed Unit Weight of Concrete in Stability Analysis
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex C.4.4 - unit weight of concrete used to compute the weight of the dam structure.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Assumed Silt Pressure
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Annex C.4.2 - assumed silt loading used in structural stability analysis.

entries.title: PAES 613 — Maximum Drop Height for a Vertical Drop Diversion Dam
entries.description: PAES 613:2016 Table 1 - maximum permissible drop height (weir crest to downstream apron) for a Vertical Drop type diversion dam.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Table 1: Classification of Check Dams
entries.table_content:
Type | Material | Bed Characteristics | Dam and Spillway
Brushwood Check Dam | Posts and brush | Gradient 5%-12%; depth < 1 m; length <= 100 m; catchment area <= 1 ha | Max dam height 1 m; upstream/downstream face inclination 30% backwards; spillway form concave or rectangular
Log Check Dam | Logs, posts, planks, heavy boards, slabs, poles or old railroad ties | Length <= 100 m; catchment area <= 2 ha | Max dam height 1.5 m; face inclination 25% backwards; rectangular spillway; spillway length 1-2 m; spillway depth 0.5-0.6 m
Loose Stone Check Dam | Relatively small rocks | Length <= 100 m; catchment area <= 2 ha | Max dam height 1.5 m; foundation depth >= 0.5 m; downstream face inclination 20%; upstream face vertical; dam thickness at spillway level 0.5-0.7 m
Boulder Check Dam | Boulders | Length <= 900 m; catchment area <= 20 ha | Max dam height 2 m; foundation depth >= 0.5 x dam height; downstream face inclination 30%; upstream face vertical; dam thickness at spillway level 0.7-10 m; trapezoidal spillway
Masonry Check Dam | Cement mortar and non-disintegrating stones | Length > 900 m; catchment area > 20 ha | Computations shown in Section 5.2
Gabion Check Dam | Gabions | Length > 900 m; catchment area > 20 ha | Computations shown in Section 5.3
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Design of a Check Dam - Table 1, classification of check dams by construction material with design/site limits.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Check Dam Spillway Discharge
entries.formula: Q = C x L x D^(3/2)
entries.variables: Q = maximum discharge of the catchment area at the check dam, m3/s. C = coefficient (3.0 for loose rock, boulder, log and brushwood check dams; 1.8 for gabion and cement masonry check dams). L = length of spillway, m. D = depth of spillway, m.
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.1.2 - spillway sizing formula common to all check dam types.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Gabion Check Dam Dimensions (3 m to 5 m Height)
entries.variables: k = thickness of the dam's crest at spillway level, m. d = thickness of the dam's base, m. f = depth of foundation, m. H = total height of the dam including foundation, m.
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.2.2 - sizing formulas for gabion check dams 3 m to 5 m in total height.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Masonry Check Dam Base Thickness (Hoffman Formula, 2 m to 6 m Height)
entries.variables: d = thickness of the dam's base, m. H = total height of the dam including foundation, m.
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.3.2 - Hoffman formula for masonry check dam base thickness when total height is 2 m to 6 m.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Masonry Check Dam Crest Thickness (6 m to 8 m Height)
entries.variables: k = thickness of the dam's crest at spillway level, m. H = total height of the dam including foundation, m.
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.3.3 - crest thickness formula for masonry check dams 6 m to 8 m in total height.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Maximum Height of a Brushwood Check Dam
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Table 1 - maximum dam height for a brushwood-type check dam.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Maximum Height of Log and Loose Stone Check Dams
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Table 1 - maximum dam height for log check dams and loose stone check dams.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Maximum Height of a Boulder Check Dam
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Table 1 - maximum dam height for a boulder check dam.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Masonry Check Dam Crest Thickness (Height Less Than 2 m)
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.3.1 - required crest thickness for masonry check dams less than 2 m in total height.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Portland Cement Mortar Mix for the First Masonry Check Dam
entries.value: 250 kg cement per m3 of sand (mortar ratio 1:4 or 1:5 by weight)
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.3.5 - mortar mix requirement for the first masonry check dam body when built on a reinforced concrete base.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Minimum Foundation Depth of the First Masonry Check Dam
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.3.5 - minimum foundation depth if the first masonry check dam is not built on solid rock (a 20 cm reinforced concrete layer is also required).

entries.title: PAES 614 — Minimum Wing Entry Into Gully Sides
entries.value: Gabion check dam: 50 cm; Masonry check dam: 1 m
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Sections 5.2.9 and 5.3.7 - minimum depth wings must enter into each side of the gully.

entries.title: PAES 614 — Aqueduct and Drainage Hole Sizing for Masonry Check Dams
entries.value: Aqueduct diameter 20 to 50 cm; drainage hole diameter at least 10 cm
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.3.8 - aqueduct and drainage hole dimensions built into masonry check dams (vertical/horizontal hole spacing 1 m and 2 m; gradient 5%).

entries.title: PAES 614 — Gabion Box Lacing Interval for 2 m Long Box Gabions
entries.description: PAES 614:2016 Section 5.2.4 - after a 2 m long box gabion is one-third full, 5 parallel ties are placed between the inner and outer sides; 5 more at two-thirds full, plus 4 corner ties.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Required Pump Discharge
entries.variables: Qr = required pump discharge, lps. IWR = irrigation water requirement, lps. h = number of hours of operation, h.
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 7.1.2 - required pump discharge from the irrigation water requirement (per PAES 602).

entries.title: PAES 615 — Maximum Sustained Yield, Confined Aquifer
entries.formula: Qs = 2 x pi x k x b x (h2 - h1) / ln(r2/r1)
entries.variables: Qs = maximum sustained yield, m3/s. k = hydraulic conductivity, m/s. b = aquifer thickness, m (T = kb = transmissivity). h2, h1 = piezometric water levels at r2 and r1, m. r2, r1 = distance from pumping well to observation wells 2 and 1, m.
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 7.1.3.1 - steady-state sustained yield for a confined aquifer.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Maximum Sustained Yield, Unconfined Aquifer
entries.formula: Qs = pi x k x (h2^2 - h1^2) / ln(r2/r1)
entries.variables: Qs = maximum sustained yield, m3/s. k = hydraulic conductivity, m/s. h2, h1 = piezometric water levels at r2 and r1, m. r2, r1 = distance from pumping well to observation wells 2 and 1, m.
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 7.1.3.1 - steady-state sustained yield for an unconfined aquifer.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Pipe Length Estimation for a Single Borehole
entries.variables: E = pipe stick-up above ground surface, m. D = depth to static water level, m. B = aquifer thickness, m. %penetration = extent of aquifer penetration (Table 5).
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 8.4 - total pipe length for a single borehole; at least 1.2 m (4 ft) is added for pump nipples.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Total Dynamic Head
entries.variables: TDH = total dynamic head, m. SWL = static water level, m. Hf = friction losses in the pipes, m (Table 4). DD = maximum drawdown when pumping at the design discharge, m. Hsf = 0.6 m (2 ft), to account for other head losses.
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 10.1.1 - total dynamic head used to size the pump.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Pump Brake Horsepower
entries.variables: BHP = brake horsepower, kW. TDH = total dynamic head, m. Qd = design pump discharge, lps. Ep = pump efficiency (assumed 55%).
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 10.1.2 - brake horsepower computation for prime mover selection.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Maximum Depth Defining a Shallow Tubewell
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 3.5 - a shallow tubewell is usually set at a depth less than 15 m, within the capability of a suction lift pump.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Well Pipe Perforation Slot Dimensions
entries.value: 3 to 6 mm width, 60 to 90 mm length
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 8.5.1 - cut with an oxyacetylene torch as vertical slots around pipe sections penetrating water-bearing formations.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Minimum Total Slot Opening Area
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 8.5.2 - minimum total area of perforation slot openings on the well pipe.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Minimum Gravel Pack Thickness (Uniform or Graded Pack)
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 9.1.2.2 - minimum gravel envelope thickness where uniformly graded or graded gravel pack is needed (UC < 2.0 or ES < 0.30 mm).

entries.title: PAES 615 — Additional Pipe Length Allowance for Nipples
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 8.4 - minimum additional pipe length added to accommodate nipples for the pumping unit installation.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Minimum Air Pressure for Well Development
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 9.5.3 - sustained air pressure released via air compressor to surge and clear a well during development.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Head Loss Allowance for Other Losses (Hsf)
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 10.1.1 - fixed allowance in the total dynamic head (TDH) formula to account for miscellaneous head losses.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Assumed Pump Efficiency
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 10.1.2 - pump efficiency value assumed in the brake horsepower (BHP) formula.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Practical Suction Lifting Range
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 9.2.4.2 - depth used as a rule of thumb for perforating pipe when aquifer hydraulic characteristics are unknown.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Minimum Thickness of a Good Confined Aquifer
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Annex A.2 - minimum thickness for an aquifer dominated by gravel and sand to be considered a good confined aquifer during well logging.

entries.title: PAES 615 — Maximum Gravel Pack Particle Size (Graded Pack)
entries.description: PAES 615:2016 Section 9.1.2.3.2 - upper size limit for graded gravel pack material (UC greater than 2.0, ES less than 0.30 mm).
